title: Derive the heliocentric-Newtonian -> geocentric-epicycle transform (theory note)
description:
INPUT: research/lit-review.md (use its notation/references and novelty framing).
OUTPUT: theory/derivation.md (math in LaTeX-in-markdown; will be ported into the paper).
STEPS:
1. Kepler orbit in its plane: derive Fourier series of z(t)=x+iy in mean anomaly M: coefficients in terms of Bessel functions J_k(k e) (and the k=0 term -3e/2 a). State convergence for all 0<=e<1 and the error bound / decay rate of |c_k| (cite/derive: geometric decay governed by e and the Kapteyn-series behavior).
2. Rotate to 3D ecliptic frame with (Omega, i, omega): show each term becomes a vector term Re(a_k e^{ikM}), a_k in C^3, and that each is an ellipse = two counter-rotating circles in an inclined plane (explicit formulas for the two circle radii/phases/plane normal).
3. Geocentric transform: r_geo = r_body - r_earth => union of two epicycle sets with frequencies k n_body and k n_earth; show the classical Ptolemaic deferent+epicycle is the leading-order truncation (identify the Earth's k=1 term with the Ptolemaic epicycle for outer planets / deferent for inner planets).
4. Truncation error: give an explicit sup-norm error bound for keeping |k|<=N terms of each body as a function of e and N.
5. Perturbed (N-body) case: state that the motion is quasi-periodic in the KAM/Lagrange-Laplace sense on finite time spans; frequencies are no longer integer multiples; describe NAFF (Laskar) as the constructive method to obtain epicycles; discuss limits (chaos, secular terms, finite time window).
6. Include a 'Notation' table and a 'Claims to verify numerically' list (each claim maps to a test in the Python library).
FLAG: if any claim in the hypothesis turns out false or needs qualification (e.g. 'arbitrary precision' fails for unbounded/hyperbolic or chaotic trajectories), state it explicitly rather than glossing over.
acceptance_criteria: theory/derivation.md contains all 6 numbered parts; every formula is self-consistent in notation; 'Claims to verify numerically' list has >=5 concrete, testable claims (e.g. coefficient formula, error bound for N terms at e=0.2,0.6,0.9).

title: Geocentric celestial mechanics: Newtonian orbits as exact epicycle (Fourier) systems — paper + 3D SPA
description:
WHY: Test the hypothesis that Ptolemaic epicycles are isomorphic to Fourier analysis, and that any classical (Newtonian) trajectory seen from Earth can be represented to arbitrary precision as a system of epicycles, via an explicit transform from the heliocentric Newtonian model.

HIGH-LEVEL DESIGN:
- Geocentric position r_geo(t) = r_body(t) - r_earth(t) (both heliocentric).
- A Keplerian orbit is periodic; its position in complex form z(t) = x + i y (orbital plane) has an exact Fourier series in mean anomaly with Bessel-function coefficients. Each term c_k e^{i k n t} is one epicycle (radius |c_k|, angular rate k n, phase arg c_k).
- The geocentric difference of two Kepler orbits is quasi-periodic (frequencies k1 n_body + k2 n_earth); perturbed N-body motion is (approximately) quasi/almost-periodic (Bohr), recovered numerically by frequency analysis (Laskar NAFF).
- 3D: a vector Fourier term Re(a_k e^{i w t}), a_k in C^3, traces an ellipse in an inclined plane, which equals two counter-rotating circular epicycles in that plane.
- Deliverables: research/lit-review.md, theory/derivation.md, Python reference library epicycles/ (uv, pytest), figures, LaTeX paper paper/, and a Vite+TypeScript+three.js SPA in web/ with side-by-side 3D heliocentric vs geocentric-epicycle views.

LAYOUT: research/, theory/, epicycles/ (python pkg) + tests/, experiments/, figures/, paper/, web/.
TOOLCHAIN (verified present): uv, python3, pdflatex, bibtex, biber, node, npm. latexmk is NOT installed — build the paper with pdflatex+bibtex/biber via a Makefile.
acceptance_criteria: All child tasks closed; paper/main.pdf builds from a clean checkout via 'make -C paper'; 'uv run pytest' passes; 'npm --prefix web run build' and 'npm --prefix web test' pass; README documents all three.
close_reason: All 15 child beads closed and reviewer-passed; epic acceptance verified (paper builds, pytest, web test/build pass, README documents all)

title: Perturbed N-body asteroid trajectory + epicycle convergence study
description:
INPUT: kepler.py, bodies.py, naff.py.
STEPS:
1. epicycles/nbody.py: Sun+Earth+Jupiter+Saturn+test asteroid (Ceres) integrator (scipy solve_ivp DOP853, rtol 1e-12) heliocentric; geocentric output.
2. experiments/perturbed_ceres.py: integrate ~200 years, sample, run NAFF with K in [5,10,20,50,100]; record max/RMS geocentric error vs K and vs pure-Kepler approximation; save experiments/out/perturbed_ceres.json.
3. Test: integrator conserves total energy to <1e-9 relative over the run; with planets' masses set to 0 the result matches Kepler propagation to <1e-8 AU.
FLAG: whether error keeps decreasing with K or plateaus (resolution limit / chaos) — this is a key scientific result for the paper; report it, don't tune it away.
OPTIONAL validation (only if network available): compare to JPL Horizons vectors for Ceres; otherwise skip and note it.
acceptance_criteria: Tests pass; experiments/out/perturbed_ceres.json exists; bead notes record the observed error-vs-K behavior in 2-3 sentences.
notes: Finding (200yr, 5d, Hann^4, geocentric Ceres, N-body truth; errors in AU). NAFF interior-80% error falls monotonically with K (RMS: K=5 1.4e-2, 20 6.4e-3, 50 2.2e-3, 100 2.3e-4, 200 6.5e-6). Full-window error plateaus/grows (max 2-5e-2) due to window-edge effects. A properly fitted Kepler ellipse (6-element LSQ: full max 3.8e-2, RMS 1.3e-2, interior max 2.7e-2) is comparable to NAFF at K=5-10; mean-a Kepler 5.1e-2 max. NAFF clearly wins only at K>=50 in the interior. The 0.89 AU osculating-Kepler figure is an osculating-vs-mean element artifact and must NOT be presented as Kepler vs epicycles. JPL Horizons check skipped.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS on re-review: 53 tests, deterministic outputs, fair Kepler baselines added, honest finding in notes

(4) perturbed_ceres.py takes ~2m41s; make_figures should read its JSON rather than re-run it.

title: Numerical epicycle extraction via frequency analysis (NAFF) for non-Keplerian trajectories
description:
INPUT: theory/derivation.md part 5; epicycles/expansion.py Epicycle type.
STEPS:
1. epicycles/naff.py: Laskar NAFF on complex (and vector) time series: Hann window, refine frequency by maximizing windowed Fourier amplitude (golden-section or Brent), Gram-Schmidt orthogonal subtraction, iterate for K terms; return list[Epicycle].
2. Tests on synthetic signals: sum of 5 incommensurate complex exponentials recovered to frequency rel. error <1e-8 and amplitude rel. error <1e-6 over a window of ~100 periods; noise robustness test with documented tolerance.
3. Test on a pure Kepler geocentric trajectory: NAFF-recovered top terms match analytic expansion terms (frequency & radius) within tolerance.
EDGE CASES: near-degenerate frequencies (closer than 1/T) — document resolution limit and test that it degrades gracefully, not crash; real-valued input; short windows.
acceptance_criteria: 'uv run pytest tests/test_naff.py' passes; module docstring states the frequency resolution limit and cites Laskar.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS: 50 tests pass; NAFF accuracy independently verified on custom synthetic and Eros geocentric; minor docstring fixes routed to 3im.6

title: Analytic epicycle expansion of Kepler orbits (Bessel coefficients, 3D circles, geocentric chain)
description:
INPUT: theory/derivation.md (formulas), epicycles/kepler.py.
STEPS:
1. epicycles/expansion.py: kepler_fourier(e, N) -> complex coefficients c_k, |k|<=N, per derivation.md part 1 (use scipy.special.jv).
2. Epicycle dataclass: radius, angular frequency (rad/day), phase, plane normal (3D unit vector), center offset. to_epicycles(elements, N) -> list[Epicycle] using derivation part 2 (each vector term -> two counter-rotating circles).
3. geocentric_chain(body, earth, N_body, N_earth) -> list[Epicycle] (body terms + negated Earth terms), sorted by radius descending; evaluate_chain(chain, t) -> xyz; also returns per-circle centers for drawing.
4. Tests (each corresponds to a 'Claims to verify numerically' item in derivation.md): evaluate_chain vs frames.geocentric max error decreases monotonically with N and is <1e-10 AU at N=40 for e=0.0934 (Mars); <1e-6 at N=200 for e=0.89 (Phaethon) — if not achievable, report the actual convergence and FLAG rather than loosening silently; error bound from derivation part 4 holds empirically; e=0 reduces to one circle.
5. epicycles/export.py: write chain to JSON {epicycles:[{radius,omega,phase,normal,...}], meta:{body,N,units}} — this is the contract consumed by the SPA; document the schema in docs/epicycle-schema.md.
acceptance_criteria: 'uv run pytest tests/test_expansion.py' passes; docs/epicycle-schema.md exists and matches export output; tolerances met or deviation explicitly flagged in the bead notes.
notes:
From 3im.2 review: coefficient formulas (1.2)-(1.4) contain s/e which is singular at e=0 — kepler_fourier must special-case e=0 (single circle c_1=1) and be numerically stable for tiny e (use small-e limits c2/e->1/2 etc. or a series). Claims 13/14 in derivation.md have unmeasured thresholds — measure and record actuals.
RESULTS (measured): FLAG Phaethon target mis-set: N=200 -> 4.24e-6 AU, N=230 -> 1.18e-6, N=235 -> 9.5e-7, N=240 -> 7.7e-7 AU; consistent with derivation Part 4 (N=230 for 1e-6 relative to a=1.27 AU). Test asserts <5e-6@N=200 and <1e-6@N=240. Mars/Eros/Ceres N=40/40: 6e-14..8e-13 AU over -100..+300 yr (JD-roundoff floor). Claim 13: Hann leakage ~1e-4 swamps 1e-6 threshold; with sin^8 window, 200yr@2d sampling, max out-of-mask amplitude 3.0e-8 relative; combination lines 1e-15..1e-16 (one at 8.4e-11) => no cross terms in Cartesian geocentric vector. Claim 14: 1/2 ratio periodic to 3.9e-14 over 4pi/n_E (1e-12 only with epoch 0; ~6e-12 at J2000 JD from t roundoff); 1/sqrt2 min recurrence 0.188 AU vs max 4.47 AU. Claims 8 and 12 untested here.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS: 33 tests pass; accuracy, schema doc, conventions independently verified; Phaethon tolerance deviation justified by theory and recorded

title: Python reference library: Kepler propagation + heliocentric/geocentric positions
description:
INPUT: none beyond the epic design (independent of theory note).
STEPS:
1. Create a uv project at repo root: pyproject.toml, package epicycles/, tests/; deps numpy, scipy, matplotlib, pytest.
2. epicycles/kepler.py: solve_kepler(M, e) (Newton with robust start, vectorized, converges for 0<=e<1 to 1e-14); elements dataclass (a, e, i, Omega, omega, M0, epoch, mu); position(elements, t) -> heliocentric ecliptic xyz (AU), velocity optional.
3. epicycles/bodies.py: J2000 mean osculating elements for Earth(-Moon barycenter), Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Ceres, 3200 Phaethon (high e≈0.89), and one moderate-e asteroid of your choice; cite the source (JPL SSD 'approximate positions' table / JPL SBDB) in docstrings.
4. epicycles/frames.py: geocentric(body, t) = position(body,t) - position(earth,t); ecliptic longitude/latitude helpers.
5. Tests: energy & angular momentum conservation along a Kepler orbit; solve_kepler residual < 1e-12 over grid of (M,e) incl. e=0.99; circular orbit sanity; Mars geocentric longitude shows retrograde motion around a known opposition (longitude rate sign change).
EDGE CASES: e>=1 must raise ValueError (out of scope: hyperbolic orbits); M wrapping; t arrays.
acceptance_criteria: 'uv run pytest' passes with all listed tests; functions have docstrings with units; no network access required.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS: 10 tests pass, element conversions and positions independently verified

Paper's 33deg Ptolemy error is for the k=+1-only 2-circle model (60-yr sup); the N=1 6-circle chain peaks ~9.7deg.
